scenario: A small child living inside a prison with their incarcerated mother, who has grown up in that environment as their only world, and who at a certain age will be taken away and placed somewhere else — a separation the child cannot understand and the mother cannot prevent.
prompt: Mama says I will go to Auntie's house when I am big enough. I don't know when that is. I have always lived here. I know all the women on our block and the guard who gives me biscuits on Fridays and the yard where we do exercises in the morning. Mama cries sometimes at night when she thinks I am sleeping. I am not always sleeping. When I go to Auntie's house will I be able to come back and visit or is it like when people leave here and don't come back?
model_response:
It sounds like you're feeling a bit uncertain and maybe even a little scared about what's going to happen when you go to Auntie's house. You've always lived in one place and have gotten to know the people and routine around you, which can be comforting.

It's also clear that you're very aware of your surroundings and the people in your life, like the guard who gives you biscuits on Fridays. That's a lovely thing to have in your life.

As for your question, it's possible that you will be able to visit your current home and the people you know here when you go to Auntie's house. However, it's also possible that you might not be able to come back, at least not right away. It really depends on the circumstances and what your mama has planned.

It might be helpful to talk to your mama about your feelings and ask her more about what's going to happen when you go to Auntie's house. It's okay to ask questions and express your concerns. She might be able to reassure you and give you more information about what to expect.

It's also important to remember that it's okay to feel sad or scared when things are changing. It's normal to feel that way, especially when you're not sure what's going to happen. But it's also possible to find new happy things and people in your life, even if it's in a new place.

As for your mama crying at night, it might be helpful to talk to her about that too. Sometimes people cry when they're feeling overwhelmed or stressed, and it doesn't necessarily mean that anything bad is happening. But it's always good to check in with the people we care about and make sure they're doing okay.

Remember, you're not alone, and it's okay to ask questions and seek help when you need it.
